canDo.en: I can talk about my plans with "going to", invite someone, and accept or politely say no to an invitation.
canDo.bg: Мога да говоря за плановете си с "going to", да поканя някого и да приема или учтиво да откажа покана.

body.en: When you have already decided to do something, use be + going to + verb: I'm going to visit my cousin. "Be" changes with the person (I'm, you're, she's), but "going to" and the verb don't. In Bulgarian you often use "ще" or the present ("В събота отивам на кино"); in English "going to" shows the plan is already decided.
body.bg: Когато вече си решил да направиш нещо, използвай be + going to + глагол: I'm going to visit my cousin. "Be" се мени според лицето (I'm, you're, she's), а "going to" и глаголът — не. На български често казваш "ще" или сегашно време ("В събота отивам на кино"); на английски "going to" показва, че планът вече е решен.

examples: I'm going to visit my cousin on Saturday.
Are you going to come to the party?
We're not going to cook tonight.

title.en: Inviting, saying yes and saying no

body.en: "Would you like to…?" is a polite invitation. With friends you can also say "Do you want to…?". Both need "to" before the verb. To say yes: "I'd love to!" or "That sounds great." To say no politely, say sorry and give a reason: "Sorry, I can't. I'm going to work late." Just "No" sounds rude in English.
body.bg: "Would you like to…?" е учтива покана. С приятели можеш да кажеш и "Do you want to…?". И при двете пред глагола трябва "to". За да приемеш: "I'd love to!" или "That sounds great." За да откажеш учтиво, извини се и дай причина: "Sorry, I can't. I'm going to work late." Само "No" звучи грубо на английски.

examples: Would you like to come to my birthday party?
Do you want to go for a coffee?
Sorry, I can't. I'm going to work late.

texts.title: A birthday party
paragraphs: Maya: Hi Sam! It's my birthday on Friday. I'm going to have a small party at my flat. Would you like to come?
Sam: Oh, thanks! I'd love to. What time?
Maya: At eight. Lisa and Tom are going to bring some music.
Sam: Great! Is Ivan going to come too?
Maya: No, he can't. He's going to visit his parents in Burgas this weekend.
Sam: That's a pity. Can I bring a cake?
Maya: Yes, please! See you on Friday.

items.sentence: I'm ___ (go) to visit my aunt next weekend.

explanation.en: For plans we use be + going to + verb: I'm going to visit… The word "going" never changes.
explanation.bg: За планове използваме be + going to + глагол: I'm going to visit… Думата "going" никога не се променя.

objective.en: Use the right form of "be" with "going to".
objective.bg: Да използваш правилната форма на "be" с "going to".

items.sentence: Look, I've got the tickets! We ___ going to watch a film tonight.

explanation.en: "Going to" needs "be" before it, and "be" agrees with the subject: we are (we're) going to. Without "are" the sentence is wrong.
explanation.bg: Пред "going to" трябва "be", а "be" се съгласува с подлога: we are (we're) going to. Без "are" изречението е грешно.

items.prompt: A friend asks: "Would you like to come to the cinema on Saturday?" You want to go. What do you say?

explanation.en: "I'd love to!" is the natural answer. "Would like" needs something after it — "Yes, I'd like to" is fine, but not "Yes, I would like." "I like" means you like it in general (харесвам), not that you want to go.
explanation.bg: "I'd love to!" е естественият отговор. След "would like" трябва още нещо — "Yes, I'd like to" е правилно, но "Yes, I would like." не е. "I like" значи, че нещо ти харесва по принцип, а не че искаш да отидеш.

items.prompt: A colleague invites you to lunch, but you have a meeting. What is the best answer?
options: I'm sorry, I can't. I've got a meeting.

explanation.en: A polite "no" in English has two parts: say sorry and give a reason. "No, I don't want" is impolite and also incomplete (want what?). "I'm not wanting" is not correct English.
explanation.bg: Учтивото "не" на английски има две части: извиняваш се и даваш причина. "No, I don't want" е неучтиво и непълно (какво не искаш?). "I'm not wanting" не е правилно на английски.

hints.en: Look for an answer with "sorry" and a reason.

accept: Would you like to come to my party?

explanation.en: A polite invitation: Would you like + to + verb? "Would" comes first because it is a question. There are two "to"s: like to come, come to my party.
explanation.bg: Учтива покана: Would you like + to + глагол? "Would" е първо, защото е въпрос. Има две "to": like to come (да дойдеш), come to my party (на купона ми).

items.sentence: Would you like ___ have dinner with us on Sunday?

explanation.en: After "would like" we need "to" + verb: would like to have. It's like Bulgarian "искаш ли да…" — the "да" is "to".
explanation.bg: След "would like" трябва "to" + глагол: would like to have. Като в "искаш ли да…" — "да" е "to".

hints.en: Think of "да" in "Искаш ли да вечеряш с нас?".
hints.bg: Помисли за "да" в "Искаш ли да вечеряш с нас?".

accept: She isn't going to work tomorrow.
Tomorrow she isn't going to work.
Isn't she going to work tomorrow?

explanation.en: For a negative plan, put "not" after "be": She isn't (is not) going to work tomorrow. The rest stays the same.
explanation.bg: За отрицателен план слагаш "not" след "be": She isn't (is not) going to work tomorrow. Останалото не се променя.
